cohort: 96 obese pregnant women (48 active and 48 inactive)
finding: Obese women who were physically active during pregnancy experienced shorter labor times and were less likely to request an epidural, with the benefits more pronounced in multiparous women.
mod_finding: This study found that obese women who were physically active during pregnancy had shorter labors and were less likely to request an epidural, but there were no significant differences in cesarean delivery rates.
